subject: humanities
passage: Written versions of the Sundiata epic, which recounts the founding of the Mali Empire in the thirteenth century, can give the impression of a single fixed text. Among the griots, the hereditary bards of West Africa who have kept the epic alive, no such text exists. Each performance adapts the story to its audience and occasion, expanding some episodes and compressing others, while the core sequence of events and the genealogies remain remarkably stable. To treat any one transcription as the definitive Sundiata is therefore to ______ a living tradition: it fixes in place what griots have kept stable only by continually varying it.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The colon explains the blank: treating a transcription as definitive "fixes in place" something that stays alive through variation. The word must mean "make rigid and lifeless," turning a flexible tradition into a frozen text.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Revitalize" means bring new life to, but fixing the epic in place would take away the variation that keeps it alive.
explanation.B: Correct. "Ossify" means harden into a rigid, unchanging form, which matches a transcription that "fixes in place" a tradition that depends on variation.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Vindicate" means prove right or justify; the text criticizes treating one version as definitive, so it does not say this practice supports the tradition.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Written versions might spread the epic to new readers, but the colon explains the blank as fixing the story in place, not making it widely known.
